paragraphs: The CLC 160 uses the M271 - a 1.8-litre supercharged four-cylinder petrol engine. It was fitted from 2008 to 2011 across the CL203 generation, the coupé version of the W203 C-Class. The M271 is known for timing chain stretch and balance shaft issues over time, which is why we replace the timing chain and timing gears as standard on every CLC 160 rebuild. The CLC-Class was a short production run and is no longer in production, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road.
about.boldParagraph: We continue to rebuild and replace M256 engines for every CLC 160 on the road.

cards.body: A 3.0-litre inline-six petrol mild-hybrid engine fitted to the CLC 160 from 2023 to present. The M256 features an integrated starter-generator (ISG) and electric auxiliary compressor, making it a more modern and efficient design than the older M276 V6. We replace timing chains, bearings, water pump and gaskets as standard on every M256 rebuild.

compatibility.intro: Because the CLC range spans two distinct engine families - the M271 petrol and the OM646 diesel - fitting the wrong replacement, or assuming an M271 part will work on a diesel car, risks a compatibility problem that's expensive to unpick. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm:

compatibility.footer: This is why we always start with your registration rather than a generic CLC-Class quote - it protects you from paying for parts that don't fit your actual car.
